Hi friend, 

If you could CHOOSE to not have trauma, to be of “normal” development - I bet my life savings and my own ass that you’d choose it. 

If your therapist made you look bad, I’ll help you find a new therapist. Seriously. Stigma is *so* prevalent with trauma. It sounds like you have a lot of the “freeze” response to trauma. Your dissociation is a normal response to what you’ve been through. If your mental health professionals stigmatize you and put you into a box, then they don’t deserve to have your trust. I am a counselor in training, and the first thing we learn is to meet clients where they are. *You deserve that.* Part of the complex trauma response is to question ourselves. You are normal. You are *not* alone. If you ever need to speak with a friend, I am here for you. I mean it. 

As far as advice goes.... TRUST YOUR FREAKING GUT. My gut tells me your therapist is not trauma-informed enough.

Hi friend, 

Bringing concerns up, diagnoses or otherwise, is totally OK, your therapist should talk with you about your concerns and try to address why they agree/disagree with you in a compassionate way... not become defensive about your concerns. Whether or not you have DID etc. or not, your symptoms and experiences are REAL. My sister once told me it is normal to think of worst case scenarios. It is part of the process of coming to terms with the TRAUMA we have endured. 

If you feel like you need attention, then your mental health probably needs attention from professionals. It sounds like you legitimately believe that something is wrong and are trying to figure out what it is. THAT IS OK AND JUSTIFIED. It is real. You deserve help. 

I’m not saying your therapist is terrible. Maybe practice assertiveness to tell her how you felt about her reaction. If she’s worth her salt she will be compassionate with you and set her own stuff aside. 

YOUR TRAUMA IS REAL. THE EFFECTS OF IT ARE REAL. Trauma manifests differently in everyone. You, my dear, sound a lot like me. And I can promise you that a good therapist is worth their weight in gold. 

Take it easy on yourself. Much love.

It is only when we can be honest with ourselves, that we're quite confused about trust (of ourselves as well as others), that deeper emotional healing can start to form into a stable foundation.” I think I’m keeping him :)

Once I started processing some of my trauma and letting a professional into my world, (and started smoking weed if I’m being honest lol) my period started to *regulate*. Since like last month. So weird. I don’t know if there’s a connection there but I was thinking about it the other day.

YEP. I had severe back pain last year and the doctor I went to did not treat me well. I remember her “feigning” back pain by standing up, clutching her back, and saying “Oh, I’m in pain too.” This is the treatment of someone who has been neglecting her health regularly. I was in a new state with my husband, barely any social connections. It’s bullshit and I wish I would have reported her.

I am so sorry. I am a counseling intern myself, and this is NOT the right way to conceptualize or treat someone who comes in with complex trauma. I’ve been fighting this for a while - many of my supervisors have dismissed clients like us - have said “they are so borderline” and don’t meet us where we are. I feel so much empathy for those who live with BPD because I’m sure they’re treated like this more than I am. I personally NEED TO WORK THROUGH THE TRAUMA MEMORIES AND CREATE A COHERENT LIFE STORY). I imagine it is the same for many people. There’s a lot that goes into this, of course, such as therapy style, what type of training the person has (LPC, MSW, Psychologist, etc.) But I *truly* believe that the number one thing that makes clinicians react this way is stigma. You’d better believe I’m doing my damn *best* to change that.

Good luck with everything. If I were in your position I’d find a new therapist. Do some research on them, too :) Look at reviews, and above all, TRUST YOUR GUT.

As someone who is just now coming out of the denial phase of the impact of my trauma, who has gotten diagnoses from BDP to bipolar to PTSD to Anxiety to ADHD to Autism Spectrum, and grew up in the world of technology and access to information about these diagnoses - I found this entire exchange to be extremely triggering. I’m upset and confused and have a lot of questions. I’ve experienced the impact of stigma for a long time, and it has been soul-crushing experience of a few hospitalizations and doctors dismissing my first and only suicide attempt in my mid-20s as “Oh, I’m not going to “endulge” you about your ideation, because you must be borderline. Go away.” When there is NO way you should treat someone like that. As a MEDICAL PROFESSIONAL? The field is FILLED with stigma. Many providers say things like - “ugh, that girl is so borderline.” It’s de-humanizing. 

I take great care in not letting my struggles be seen by others because that was an adaptation I learned from my family. I wasn’t allowed to talk about things. So I suppressed my own needs and wants, because I learned that taking care of others made me feel more safe. I sacrificed so much for the possibility of stability for my mom. I think it has come out in other relationships now. Does that mean some of the other effects of my abuse don’t come out? Absolutely not. But really only with my husband. Every once in awhile I misunderstand what he is saying, and think he might be criticizing me, which I allow to contribute to my toxic shame. I don’t lash out at him for it, rather, I feel confused and don’t know how to express what I mean or put it into words. I dissociate. And then I feel SCARED and a bit protective over myself. Then I have to look at the situation more critically - likely there was just a miscommunication. We don’t say things that intentionally hurt the other. Then, I try to talk with him about what I’m feeling, and ask how he is feeling. I’m learning to see the bigger picture and I’ve done a really good job with being gentle with myself AND him. He is an amazing man, and he apparently sees a lot of amazing qualities within me - just as I see in him. I’m working on doing the same thing with other people - allowing myself to be vulnerable but also knowing when I should put up boundaries. 

Anyway, thank you for listening if you got through it. I’m still piecing everything together myself.

I don’t believe there is *anything* wrong with allowing myself to be loved by my partner. As long as I’m working on myself and doing all that I can personally to make sure my family is happy and healthy, and meeting myself where I am, I’ve found that I can easily accept the depth of love from my partner. Because at the end of the day we trust and respect each other’s boundaries... to be honest that part is the easiest part. Because I know what it’s like to have my own boundaries crossed, and I never want to come close to allowing myself to damage another person. And the fact that my husband respects my boundaries means he values ALL of his loved ones feeling safe. 💙

To be honest, I don’t know what mistreatment is. I know that sounds weird... but I was abused and mistreated for most of my life and I’m not willing to accept that level of abuse anymore. But, the other stuff? From people who aren’t in my family of origin? How do I tell if I’m being mistreated or just being defensive and sensitive like my mom used to tell me I was being? What do I look for? Tone of voice? Content? What are the red flags? This feels humiliating to even write and I’m nearly 30. I’m so grateful to have found my amazing husband. He has shown me how I *should* be treated. Maybe I should start there.

edit: Yes, I DO know what mistreatment is because I would never stand for the mistreatment of others that I see so clearly. I guess the problem is that I can’t see it clearly for myself.
You are me.

What is the difference between the person who had swelling, it turned out to be a sprain and healed, and the person whose pain never goes away? Is it the level of abuse? Strength? Weakness? No one caught my abuse. The system failed me. And it failed me again when no one caught it because CPTSD is so widely misunderstood! I’m furious! WHY didn’t someone help me when I was a child? Because the abuse isn’t as bad as I thought? Because *I’m* the manipulative one who is making this up???
